title: backlog.py cost prints item work, research and overhead apart for a sprint
goal: backlog.py cost SP prints item work, research and system overhead (the overhead lines inside the sprint's window) as separate totals

gates.question: In a sprint's cost report, are the research items' tokens taken out of the item work figures (direct, attributed, session total) and printed as a total of their own, or left in them and printed again as a part?
options: apart: taken out of item work; research is its own total (no figure counted twice)
part: stay in item work; research printed as the part of it charged to research items
gates.recommendation: apart: taken out of item work; research is its own total (no figure counted twice)
gates.answer: apart: taken out of item work; research is its own total (no figure counted twice)

gates.question: Which deterministic rule dates a sprint's window for its system overhead?
options: git: oldest commit adding status active to the sprint file (start) to the newest commit deleting it (close, open while the file exists); run time from its run id, both bounds inclusive; unresolved in a shallow clone or without git
sidecar times only: first and last run of the sprint's own work lines
gates.recommendation: git: oldest commit adding status active to the sprint file (start) to the newest commit deleting it (close, open while the file exists); run time from its run id, both bounds inclusive; unresolved in a shallow clone or without git
gates.answer: git: oldest commit adding status active to the sprint file (start) to the newest commit deleting it (close, open while the file exists); run time from its run id, both bounds inclusive; unresolved in a shallow clone or without git

notes: Scope widened: the cost row of tools.md and the Cost of work section of backlog.md describe the sprint's three totals; the push gate refuses the code without them.
